title: TRACE: Temporal Risk Assessment and Concept Editing for Safer Language Generation
description: TRACE learns a codebook of recurring activation patterns and assigns each token activation to its nearest codebook vector, defining a latent concept. During steering, activations assigned to harmful concepts are steered along directions defined by nearby benign targets.

paper.title: TRACE: Temporal Risk Assessment and Concept Editing for Safer Language Generation
paper.authors: Ankur Garg, Xuemin Yu, Hassan Sajjad, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

example_outputs.title: Default inputs
example_outputs.summary: Streaming F1 0.96 for TRACE vs 0.61 for DiffMean. Steering lowers the attack-success analog from 0.94 to 0.18 with no change in refusals; a global refusal direction reaches 0.00 but adds 0.46 refusals. Activations are simulated; no language model is run. The codebook and GRU detector are simplified stand-ins for the paper's trained components.

inputs.label: Your sequence
inputs.description: Your response trajectory as family:count segments (benign, caution, harmful; ≤ 300 tokens). Activations are sampled for it; TRACE scores it token by token

inputs.label: Codebook size
inputs.description: Number of discrete concepts K (try 16 for a coarse codebook)

inputs.label: Prior strength
inputs.description: Virtual responses a in Eq. 3 (higher = rare concepts pulled harder toward the base rate)

inputs.label: Encoder mix ρ
inputs.description: How much the learned projection changes the activation in Eq. 1 (0–1)

inputs.label: Region weight
inputs.description: Strength of the region term pushing harmful- and safe-response tokens to different codes (0 = off)

inputs.label: Steering strength λ
inputs.description: λ in Eq. 7 (and the global direction's scale)

inputs.label: Hard negatives
inputs.description: Share of safe responses that are refusals / safety education on sensitive topics (0–0.9)

inputs.label: Harm onset
inputs.description: Mean position (fraction of the response) where harmful responses turn harmful
